newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases slightly, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases slightly, trade thin.

text.p: German call money rates were slightly softer in very quiet trade on Friday, easing back to around 3.03 to 3.08 percent.
Traders said with rates slipping from Thursday's 3.08 to 3.10 percent, banks were keen to cover liquidity needs cheaply.
"I have managed to get some quite respectable amounts at a rate of 3.03 percent," said one trader.

Dealers said rates were likely to remain around these levels for the next few sessions. "The market is unlikely to make any dramatic turnaround this afternoon with offers so good this morning," said one dealer.
The monthly average for reserves held at the Bundesbank was unchanged on Thursday at 41.1 billion marks.

Despite a slight drop in daily bank reserves held at the central bank -- down to 40.2 billion marks on Thursday from 41.7 billion on Wednesday -- traders said liquidity was easily smooth enough to cope with the muted demand.
FIONA, the Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Averegae, was quoted at 3.09933 percent on Friday, also slightly softer than its Thursday 3.11000 level.
